facts.name: Program audience and curriculum focus
facts.detail: Program page: the M.S. is tailored to working professionals and is described as offering a current computing curriculum.
facts.quote: Tailored to the schedules of working professionals, the CSULB Master of Science in Computer Science program offers the most relevant and up-to-date curriculum to meet the demands of the rapidly changing world of computing.

facts.name: Advanced study areas
facts.detail: Program page: the M.S. provides advanced study in software development and engineering, networking, operating systems, distributed computing, AI, and algorithm analysis.
facts.quote: The M.S. in Computer Science provides advanced study in software development and engineering, networking, operating systems, distributed computing, artificial intelligence, and analysis of algorithms.

facts.name: Concentrations
facts.detail: Students can pursue concentrations in Advanced Systems or Software Development.
facts.quote: Students can pursue concentrations in Advanced Systems or Software Development.

facts.name: Culminating experience
facts.detail: Students finish with a comprehensive exam or a thesis research project.
facts.quote: Complete your graduate degree with a comprehensive exam or thesis research project.

facts.name: Bachelor's degree and GPA
facts.detail: MSCS admissions: bachelor's in computer engineering or computer science, or sufficient background, with a minimum 2.7 GPA in the last 60 semester or 90 quarter upper-division major units.
facts.quote: Hold a bachelor's degree in computer engineering or computer science or have sufficient background in computer engineering or computer science from a college or university with a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 2.7 in the last 60 semester or 90 quarter upper-division major units attempted.

facts.name: University graduate admission requirements
facts.detail: The MSCS admissions page also requires applicants to satisfy university requirements for graduate admission.
facts.quote: Satisfy university requirements for graduate admission

facts.name: University minimum GPA options (university-wide)
facts.detail: University-wide graduate standing page: a baccalaureate with a cumulative GPA of at least 2.5, with no rounding. This is a university rule, not an MSCS-only rule.
facts.quote: Hold a baccalaureate degree with a cumulative GPA of at least 2.5. (No Rounding)

facts.name: University master's application latest dates (not MSCS-specific)
facts.detail: University Key Dates page: master's program deadlines vary by program. This is a university-wide latest-date rule, not an MSCS-only deadline.
facts.quote: Master’s programs and certificates application deadline

facts.name: Spring 2027 master's latest date (university-wide)
facts.detail: University-wide latest date for master's applications for Spring 2027 admission: no later than Nov. 1, 2026; the page says dates vary by program.

facts.name: Fall 2027 master's latest date (university-wide)
facts.detail: University-wide latest date for master's applications for Fall 2027 admission: no later than June 1, 2027; the page says dates vary by program.
facts.quote: Varies by program (no later than June 1, 2027)

facts.name: Catalog heading
facts.detail: The 2026-2027 University Catalog program heading is Computer Science, M.S.
facts.quote: Computer Science, M.S.

facts.name: Program mission
facts.detail: The catalog describes a graduate program meant to prepare leaders in industry and also students who later pursue advanced degrees, with advanced courses in software and hardware analysis and design.
facts.quote: The mission of the graduate program in Computer Science at CSULB is to provide a high-quality educational experience and the technical specialization required to become successful leaders in industry.

facts.name: Thesis or comprehensive examination
facts.detail: Students may finish with a thesis or a comprehensive examination.
facts.quote: The students may choose to do a thesis or take a comprehensive examination as the culmination of their program.

facts.name: Admission degree background
facts.detail: Applicants need a bachelor's degree in computer engineering or computer science, or sufficient background in those fields, from a college or university.
facts.quote: To be considered for admission the graduate applicant must have earned a bachelor's degree in computer engineering, computer science or sufficient background in computer engineering or computer science from a college or university

facts.name: Admission GPA of 2.7 in last 60 semester units
facts.detail: The minimum GPA is 2.7 in the last 60 semester or 90 quarter upper-division major units attempted.
facts.quote: a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 2.7 in the last 60 semester or 90 quarter upper division major units attempted.

facts.name: Apply through Cal State Apply, not the department
facts.detail: Applications go through Cal State Apply; the page says not to send an application to the department. International students also apply at Cal State Apply.
facts.quote: The student should apply online at www.calstate.edu/apply . Do not send an application to the Department.

facts.name: Remove deficiencies before graduate-level courses
facts.detail: All deficiencies must be removed before a student attempts graduate-level courses.
facts.quote: All deficiencies must be removed before attempting graduate-level courses.

facts.name: Advancement to candidacy: deficiencies and overall GPA
facts.detail: Students applying for advancement to candidacy must have completed all undergraduate deficiencies with grades of C or better and have an overall GPA of 3.0.
facts.quote: Students applying for advancement to candidacy must: have completed all undergraduate deficiencies with grades of "C" or better; have attained an overall grade point average (GPA) of 3.0;

facts.name: Advancement to candidacy: 9 units and advisor approval
facts.detail: They must also complete at least 9 units of required degree-applicable courses with a 3.0 GPA in those units, and have a plan of study approved by the CECS department graduate advisor.
facts.quote: have completed at least 9 units of required courses applicable to the degree with a GPA of at least 3.0 for the completed units; and have their plans of studies approved by the CECS department graduate advisor.

facts.name: Degree unit total
facts.detail: The degree requires 30 units.
facts.quote: Degree Requirements (30 units)

facts.name: First-semester plan of study
facts.detail: Students must meet the Graduate Program Adviser at the start of the first semester to make a tentative plan of study. The page also says a detailed required-and-elective list is kept on the Graduate Program website.
facts.quote: Students must meet with the Graduate Program Adviser at the beginning of their first semester to create a tentative plan of study.

facts.name: Culminating options and 400-level cap
facts.detail: Students must choose the Thesis Option or the Comprehensive Exam Option. At most 9 units of 400-level coursework may count toward the degree.
facts.quote: As a culminating activity, students must elect either the Thesis Option or the Comprehensive Exam Option. A maximum of 9 units of 400-level coursework may be applied toward the degree.

facts.name: Comprehensive exam option unit split
facts.detail: The exam option requires 30 graduate hours in computer science, a passing comprehensive exam, 15 units of required core courses, and 15 units of allowed electives, with no more than 9 units from 400-level courses.
facts.quote: Student must complete 30 graduate hours credit in computer science and pass the comprehensive exam. 15 units of required core courses

facts.name: Exam-option elective units
facts.detail: Under the comprehensive exam option, students take 15 units from the allowed electives, with no more than 9 units from 400-level courses.
facts.quote: 15 units from allowed electives (No more than 9 units may be from the 400 level courses.)

facts.name: Comprehensive exam covered courses
facts.detail: The comprehensive exam covers CECS 524, CECS 528, and CECS 543. The page does not list CECS 530 or CECS 558 among the covered courses, even though those two are in the required core.
facts.quote: Comprehensive examination covering the following required courses: CECS 524 - Advanced Topics in Programming Languages (3 units) CECS 528 - Advanced Analysis of Algorithms (3 units) CECS 543 - Advanced Software Engineering (3 units)

facts.name: Thesis option unit split
facts.detail: The thesis option requires 15 units of required courses, 9 units of allowed electives (no more than 9 units from 400-level courses), and 6 units of research and thesis.
facts.quote: 15 units of required courses

facts.name: Thesis-option elective units
facts.detail: Under the thesis option, students take 9 units from allowed electives, with no more than 9 units from 400-level courses.
facts.quote: 9 units from allowed electives (No more than 9 units may be from the 400 level courses.);

facts.name: Thesis research and report
facts.detail: The thesis option includes 6 units of research and thesis with a written report and oral presentation approved by the thesis committee. At least 3 of those units must be CECS 698; the remaining 3 units may be CECS 697 or CECS 698.
facts.quote: 6 units of research and thesis with written report and oral presentation approved by the thesis committee.

facts.name: Thesis minimum from CECS 698
facts.detail: At least 3 of the 6 thesis-option research units must be taken from CECS 698 Thesis or Industrial Project.
facts.quote: At least 3 units must be taken from the following course CECS 698 - Thesis or Industrial Project (3-6 units)

facts.name: Thesis remaining 3 units
facts.detail: The remaining 3 thesis research units may be CECS 697 Directed Research or CECS 698 Thesis or Industrial Project.
facts.quote: Remaining 3 units may be taken from either of the following courses CECS 697 - Directed Research (1-3 units) CECS 698 - Thesis or Industrial Project (3-6 units)
